fields.meta_description: Take orders on a fundraiser order form, credit each one to a student seller, and add every order into one supplier order when the sale closes.
fields.h1: Build a Fundraiser Order Form That Credits Every Seller
fields.hero_description: Build a fundraiser order form that totals each order, credits the seller, and saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Paper Order Sheet Cannot Do
fields.features_subheading: A paper sheet rides home in a backpack and gets added up by hand. These six parts keep orders, sellers, and payments in one place.
fields.feature_1:
Credit for the student who made the sale

Each order names the student or player who sold it. Seller totals come from the saved orders, and a coordinator can sort the whole sale by seller, class, or team in one view.
fields.feature_2:
Items, sizes, and prices set up once

List each product with its price and options, such as scent, grind, or size. The buyer picks quantities, the total updates on the screen, and one price list runs the whole sale.
fields.feature_3:
Payment status on every order

Ask whether the buyer paid by cash, by check, or will pay at pickup. The treasurer marks an order paid when the money arrives, and the list of open balances stays current all week.
fields.feature_4:
Emails when a seller reaches a goal

Set a goal, such as 20 items, and pick who hears about it. The chair gets an email or a Slack message when a seller crosses it, and that student goes straight onto the prize list.
fields.feature_5:
Every order in a database you own

Orders save as rows in a database you own, with no cap on responses. A sale that runs past its target keeps taking orders, and next year's sale starts from this year's data.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository. A booster club or school district with its own developer can host the order form anywhere and keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Groups Run Their Sales
fields.tab_content_1:
Students who reach 20 candles land on the prize list

Brookhaven Elementary's PTA sells soy candles for its library fund. Each order names the student who sold it and the homeroom. When a student reaches 20 candles, the PTA chair, Nadia Pruitt, gets an email to add that student to the prize list.
fields.tab_content_2:
The buyer's total updates with each bag

Ridgeline Rovers, a youth soccer club, sells coffee by the bag. A buyer picks a roast, a grind, and the number of bags. Kara Linden orders 3 bags at $15, and her total reads $45.00 before she submits. Her confirmation email names Jonah Pike, the player who will deliver them.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every wreath order adds up into one supplier order

Troop 214 sells holiday wreaths in three sizes. When the sale closes, the app adds up the orders by size: 64 small, 31 medium, and 12 large, or 107 wreaths in all. Troop leader Hector Vance gets the totals in a Slack direct message and places the order with the wreath farm.
fields.tab_content_4:
The pickup table holds any unpaid order for the treasurer

Westfield High's band boosters run pickup day from a tablet, and volunteers check off each order as a family collects it. An order still marked unpaid stays at the table. By noon, 41 orders were picked up and 3 were held, and the treasurer, Gil Moreno, had an email listing each held order with its seller and the amount due.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Fundraiser Order Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a fundraiser order form that credits each seller and totals the sale, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Write down what you are selling
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the product sheet from your supplier. List every item with its price and the options buyers choose, such as scent or wreath size. Leave out anything the supplier cannot fill, because each choice on the form becomes a line on the supplier order.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick what identifies a seller: the student's name plus a homeroom, a team, or a den. Offer those names as a list instead of a text box. A typed name spelled two ways splits one seller's total into two.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Collect the buyer's name and email on every order. Ask for a street address only when sellers deliver door to door. A pickup sale needs a phone number so a volunteer can call about an order that nobody collected.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Offer the payment methods your treasurer accepts, such as cash, check, or pay at pickup. Add a paid or unpaid status to each order. The treasurer changes it when money arrives, and the pickup list reads from that status.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set a close date and seller goals
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the day the form stops taking orders, timed to your supplier's deadline. Then set any seller goals and who hears about them. A goal of 20 items and an email to the chair is a simple place to start.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Place 3 orders yourself before sharing the link: one with a single item, one with every option, and one marked unpaid. Check the totals by hand and confirm each order shows up under the right seller.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Plan pickup day before the sale ends
fields.howto_step_7_des: Decide whether orders are sorted by seller or by family, and who checks them off. Open the pickup list on a tablet and run your test orders through it. Volunteers then know how to hold an unpaid order before the first family arrives.

faq_plan.q: What is a fundraiser order form?
faq_plan.a: A fundraiser order form is the sheet or online form a group uses to take orders for the products it sells to raise money, such as candles or wreaths. Each order records the buyer, the items and quantities, the total, the payment, and the seller who gets credit for the sale.

faq_plan.q: How to create a fundraiser order form?
faq_plan.ref: how to create a fundraiser order form
faq_plan.a: List your products with prices and options, decide how sellers get credit, and add buyer contact fields and a payment status. In Emergent's AI form builder, describe the sale in one prompt, such as "candles at $18, credit each student, email the chair at 20 sold," and Emergent builds the form and the order database behind it.

faq_plan.q: Can you recommend tools for designing fundraiser order forms?
faq_plan.ref: can you recommend tools for designing fundraiser order forms
faq_plan.a: Yes: Jotform, SurveyMonkey, and AidaForm each publish a fundraiser order form template. Jotform's free template can be customized and embedded on a website, SurveyMonkey's lets supporters enter order quantities and contact details, and AidaForm offers a free editable version. Test each one against what your sale needs after an order arrives, such as seller totals.

faq_plan.q: What should a fundraiser order form template include?
faq_plan.a: Include the buyer's name and phone, each product with its price, a quantity for each item, the line total, the seller's name, and a paid or unpaid box. If the sale has one product and no sellers to credit, a general order form covers it.

faq_plan.q: Is there a fundraiser order form template I can use for free?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and its free tier covers building and publishing a form. Describe your products and sellers in a prompt, and the form comes back with its order database, ready to share with families.

faq_plan.q: How do you choose between fundraiser order form templates?
faq_plan.a: Choose by what happens after the order. Check whether each order carries a seller, whether the form shows the buyer a total, and whether all orders add up by item when the sale closes.

faq_plan.q: What should you check before using free fundraiser order form templates?
faq_plan.a: Check the response cap on the free plan and what happens to the form when the sale reaches it. Emergent puts no cap on responses. When the sale closes, use the item totals to fill in the purchase order form you send your supplier.

faq_plan.q: How do you fill out a blank fundraiser order form?
faq_plan.a: Write the seller's name at the top, then give each buyer one row: name, phone, the quantity of each item, and the row total. Mark paid or unpaid in the last column as money comes in, and add up the columns before you turn the sheet in.

faq_plan.q: Can I turn a blank fundraiser order form template into an online form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. List the template's columns in a prompt to Emergent, with the prices and the seller field, and it builds an online form with the same fields. Every order then lands in a database you own, ready to sort by seller.

faq_plan.q: What does a brick fundraiser order form need to collect?
faq_plan.a: It needs the exact inscription for each brick, line by line, with a character limit per line that matches what your engraver accepts. Add the brick size and the buyer's contact details. Treat it like a t shirt order form with custom printing: the buyer confirms the spelling before submitting.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries (Jotform, SurveyMonkey, AidaForm, Formsite, 123FormBuilder) and printable sheets (Pinterest, Etsy, sampletemplates). Every one stops at the order line on a single sheet. This page shows the parts a paper sheet cannot do for a group sale: credit each order to the student seller, total each buyer's order, add every order into one supplier order when the sale closes, and run pickup day with paid and unpaid orders apart. Four groups a searcher will recognize: an elementary PTA candle sale, a youth soccer coffee sale, a scout troop wreath sale, and a high school band pickup day. The FAQ answers the definition, how to build one, tools, templates (free and blank), how a seller fills one out, and brick sales.
